model.name: All Tasks owned by the owner profile — scoped backfill that preserves every structural parent (Task and non-Task)
model.description: Tron's Set-as-Current on Task 40.1 returned 403 'owner only' because that Task's ownerIor is null. His rule: EVERY Task is owned by his profile (05e58f81 'Marcel Donges'). ownerIor is OVERLOADED: profile-owner on a Task, STRUCTURAL PARENT on chain units (Impl->Method, CR->Test). LOCKED SPLIT (reciprocation test, 525 Tasks): A(direct)=206 [195 null + 11 dual-carriers -> set owner directly] / B(relocate)=220 [old-schema the Sprint RECIPROCATES -> relocate Sprint ownerIor->model.parent] / D(set-owner-only, ORPHANS)=99 [old-schema NO sprint claims -> set owner, DROP stale pointer, NO relocation] / C=0 / anomaly=0. The 99 orphans MUST NOT be relocated: copying a stale ownerIor into model.parent would FABRICATE a parent the named sprint does not acknowledge (drawer says 'parent Sprint X' while overview shows it unsorted) = 99 fresh drift instances. A migration must NEVER fabricate a link to satisfy its own rule. The backfill touches NO non-Task ownerIor.
model.crossRefNote: R40.17 owner-gate (the 403 Set-as-Current path); R40.10 owner identity via profile (05e58f81 = the same owner-profile-unit that approvedBy uses). The re-parent we did today (CR->Test) is the exact ownerIor-is-structural case the scope-AC must not disturb.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every ior:class:Task has ownerIor = the owner profile 05e58f81 (Marcel Donges), so the Set-as-Current owner-gate passes for the owner (T40.1's 403-while-null is resolved).

The backfill modifies ownerIor on ior:class:Task units ONLY. NO non-Task unit's ownerIor is modified — Impl->Method, ChangeRequest->Test, Requirement->Sprint etc. are STRUCTURAL parents, left untouched.
A seeded NON-Task unit whose ownerIor would change under the backfill => RED. (Without this, a correct-looking backfill silently destroys the traceability graph.)

RELOCATION (Case B = 220 tasks) applies ONLY to old-schema tasks the Sprint RECIPROCATES (lists in Sprint.tasks[]): copy the Sprint from ownerIor into model.parent FIRST, then set ownerIor=owner-profile — the Sprint acknowledges them, so the parent is real. Post-backfill these keep ownerIor=owner-profile AND parent=their Sprint AND remain in Sprint.tasks[].
A reciprocated Task (Case B) that loses its Sprint linkage after the backfill (parent unset AND absent from Sprint.tasks[]) => RED.

Gated dry-run + before/after counts (525 Tasks: 195 null->owned, 330 Sprint-in-ownerIor->parent-relocated-then-owned), reversible, ambiguous->flag; the owner profile uuid is not leaked into logs beyond the unit field.

The owner value is the owner profile UNIT (05e58f81), resolved SINGLE-SOURCE (profileUuidOf(owner) / the owner profile), not a literal scattered across call sites — the owner-gate reads the same source it is backfilled from.

The 99 Case-D ORPHANS (old-schema, NO sprint reciprocates) get owner set + the stale ownerIor DROPPED, and are NOT relocated. Relocating a stale pointer into model.parent would FABRICATE a parent the named Sprint denies = 99 new drift. They were already unsorted, so nothing visible regresses; re-homing is R40.51. stub-must-fail: a migration that sets model.parent on an orphan to a Sprint whose tasks[] does not list it => RED. Architect-confirmed post-apply invariant (quote, fd8c968af): for the 99 D-orphans, model.parent stays ABSENT AND ownerIor==05e58f81 (owner set, stale ownerIor->Sprint DROPPED, NO model.parent written; they remain honestly unsorted).
--apply stays GATED until the expert dry-run ADDS the reciprocation check and REPRODUCES A=206/B=220/D=99/C=0/anomaly=0 exactly, then the architect clears it. Not "unblocked" on the split alone.
